## Strategist — Sanctum Seeker in, Giver of Runes out
Correction: Pact of the Serpent is {1}{B}{B} sorcery, "target player draws X and loses X life, X = creatures THEY control of the chosen type" — no each-opponent drain, no five-mana slot. Champion of Dusk {3}{B}{B} Vampire: ETB draw X lose X (X = your Vampires). Idol of Oblivion {2}: tap, draw if you made a token this turn.
1. Why Seeker left: branch.json staged[6] 2026-11-11, out Seeker in Elas il-Kor, why "every Edgar token gains 1 (Vito/Bond drain), every death drains" — a judgment on Elas, none on Seeker; the pilot never rejected Seeker. Recon: 71.1% of B3 lists, in a combat-swarm-with-drain-rider consensus. Trigger on attack: each opponent loses 1, you gain 1, per attacking Vampire, blocks irrelevant; stack 003 (Bloodletter + Seeker) is checker-passed scaling (strategy:aristocrats.drain-scope). "At a distance" only in the weak sense (needs no block to connect) but needs Vampires alive to attack; Deluge/Meathook/Skeleton loops do not feed it. It is the one repeatable gain-linked drain that works WITHOUT a death.
2. Draw candidates (strategy:card-advantage.plan-draw): Champion of Dusk is the best draw add (Vampire body, burst, life priced against the drain refund) — a separate card 6; Pact is cheaper but no body/no eminence; Idol one card a turn. None beats Seeker's slot value.
3. Weakest slots: Giver of Runes (non-Vampire, 1 MV, protects only others, dies to the first wipe; Spirit/Charm/Teferi's/Tenacity cover the job); Preacher of the Schism (attack-conditional draw; cut candidate if Seeker returns since both want attackers — though note Seeker + Preacher both reward attacking). Morbid Opportunist is NOT a cut (best draw rate per slot); Reassembling Skeleton is NOT (stack 013). Sac outlets: Altar, Seer, Yahenni, Tower = 4 + Spirit self-sac.
4. Recommendation: Seeker for Giver. Pairs with Teysa (x2), Bloodletter (x2), Vito/Bond (x3). Fallback if protection is kept: Seeker for Preacher. Next: Champion of Dusk for Preacher; then Pact for the weakest non-Vampire body.
Open: ledger note on whether Seeker's cut was the thesis or the Elas swap; strategy topic "attack-trigger drains in a non-combat plan".

Asked: after Black Market Connections, Malakir Bloodwitch, Clever Concealment and Lethal Scheme, the ONE next upgrade to threat-v1 and the card it replaces, with Sanctum Seeker (A) and Pact of the Serpent (B) leading. The answer is Sanctum Seeker for Falkenrath Noble. Cards 1-4 bought draw shape, a finisher body, a wipe answer and free removal; what the log still shows is a wide board that does not close before the next wipe — 006 'got a wider board, bigger +1/+1 counters, and just couldn't convert before the next wipe', 001 lost with Alex on 1 life when the pilot 'needed one more vampire and had nothing'. Enumerated from the branch's 64 non-lands: no card drains per ATTACKING Vampire (the three with attack text are Preacher of the Schism, Crossway Troublemakers and the commander's own counters); every repeatable drain the branch owns either consumes a body (eight death-drains, ten repeatable outlets) or waits on a gain, an entry, an arrival or an upkeep. Seeker is the one candidate in the brief's list that turns board WIDTH into an each-opponent drain every turn without spending the fuel, and it is non-combat in the pilot's own sense (006: 'ways to assign damage that is not combat damage') — the loss is a trigger on declaration, blockers and indestructible never see it (checker-passed stack 003: seven attackers with Bloodletter drained each opponent 14 'before blockers are even declared'). Noble is the cut because it is the eighth death-drain and the one in the lowest yield quadrant (targeted, 1 per event, four mana) while Blood Artist does the same job at two; no checker-passed stack names it. Pact is the runner-up, and the question's premise about it is wrong: Pact costs {1}{B}{B}, three mana, not five — Champion of Dusk is the five. Pact does not compete with Edgar's six-mana turn, and aimed at an opponent naming THEIR type it is a kill through indestructible that nobody in the brief mentioned. It is second, not first, because its self-cast refuel reads the board the wipe just took and the deck's recorded failure is conversion, not count: the branch already holds ten draw sources by oracle text. No goldfish figure appears here, by the pilot's ruling; every count is from the branch decklist, its cards.json (sha a78d3f55…, current), card_roles.json and oracle text.
